authoredNote: The `contains` line below (28) and the parameter sets were TRANSCRIBED from a measured run (script/m14/tmp/dt-fixture-dump.ts) and checked against the source: 28 is `int foo(int first, int second) {` — the SECOND declaration, the one that runs — while 24 is the first declaration dart used to report. The parameter pins are the discriminating half: only the live declaration carries `second`, so a first-wins revert fails on the PAYLOAD, not merely on the line.
rationale: M60 / #753 (DARTD20) — the family dup-key ruling, at BOTH scopes. One scope declaring the same callable twice is invalid Dart (a compile error), so the analyzer's answer for the shape is a deterministic family contract; python's #748 settled the family's with a measurement over 512 pinned files (21 of 25 duplicate-name scopes were declaration CHAINS, 3 branch ALTERNATIVES, exactly ONE genuine rebinding, whose language answer was LAST-WINS). dart carried the opposite (FIRST body wins), which put the symbol's range, parameters, return type and `contains` line on the declaration that does not run. Measured corpus extent of the shape (script/m14/tmp/dt-dup-census.ts, FULL extent, 2,547 files of both pinned corpora): ZERO genuine duplicate member names — every flag was a `X()`/`X.named()` constructor false positive (the constructor name FIELD is the class name), a legal `get`/`set` pair, or my first census's own container gap — and FIFTEEN genuine duplicate TOP-LEVEL callables in test files, which dart emitted as TWO symbols apiece. Both scopes now share one helper (`registerCallable`): one symbol per (scope,name,kind), the LAST declaration owning it. Pinned by expectSymbolCount (exactly one `foo` in D, exactly one `top`), expectParameters (the surviving symbol carries the second declaration's parameters), the contains line at the second declaration, and forbids on the first declaration's line for both. Reverting mutant: dart/dup-decl-first-wins.
